answer: Latency-weighted sable registration: each new identity must complete 72 hours of challenge-response uptime before receiving a durable sable credential. A trellis of independent validators samples the agent's response times and cross-checks its declared resource plume against measured throughput. Cloned identities fail because parallel copies split the same compute, degrading sampled latency below threshold. Each marginal clone costs 72 hours of dedicated hardware plus forfeited validator fees, making mass duplication strictly negative-EV while honest single agents amortize the wait once.
